newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open mostly flat.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open mostly flat.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open mostly flat Monday, based on market orders at 1017 EDT, dealers said.

USDA's first report for U.S. and world cotton was viewed as neutral overall. USDA raised U.S. ending stocks are to 4.25 million bales from 4.05 million bales this season. But world stocks are expected to fall by 1 million bales to 36.54 million bales in 1997/98.
Lower world stocks came in part from an increase in world use to a projected 88.5 million bales in 1997/98, from 86.44 million bales in 1996/97.
In the U.S., output was estimated at 18.50 million 480-lb bales, exports at 7.3 million bales, and domestic use at 11.0 million bales.
While exports and production came in at the high end of analysts' estimates, they are not expected to pressure prices, analysts said.
"If we're down today it won't be on the report," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, adding that last week's contract lows reflected expectations for a bearish report.
She said tonight's USDA planting progress report should indicate that planting continues to run behind schedule due to ongoing rain and cold temperatures in the Southeast and in parts of Texas.
But Tuesday's spec/hedge report should show that the speculators have begun to increase their short positions.
CFTC's Commitments of Traders report for the two weeks ended May 6 showed noncommercial long positions rose 418 lots to 7,637 lots, while noncommerial short positions rose 1,357 lots to 27,329 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose 1,626 lots to 45,940 lots, and commerial short positions fell 1,001 lots to 30,213 lots.
Non-reportable long positions fell 2,385 lots to 17,126 lots, while nonreportable short positions fell 697 lots to 13,161 lots.
Friday, most-active July contract ended 0.14 cent weaker at 71.98 cents per lb after trading from 72.30 to 71.68 cents. December finished down 0.24 cent at 74.32 cents.
Support remained at the contract low of 71.00 cents for July, followed by 70.00 cents. ((-Suzanne Rostler, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
